messages.content:
Here is the complete worked solution following official CAPS marking guidelines (5 marks):

Marking criteria:
(a) Substitution of 63,5 into $n = \frac{m}{M} \checkmark$
(b) Substitute $6{,}02 \times 10^{23}\text{ mol}^{-1} \checkmark$
(c) $n(\text{electrons}) = N(\text{Cu atoms}) \times 2$ OR $n(\text{electrons}) = N(\text{Cu atoms}) \times 1 \checkmark$
(d) Calculate $t = (5)(60)(60) = 18\,000\text{ s} \checkmark$
(e) Final correct answer: $2{,}68\text{ A} \checkmark$ (Range: 1,34 to 2,70 A)

USING $\text{Cu}^{2+}$:
$$n(\text{Cu}) = \frac{m}{M} = \frac{16}{63{,}5} \checkmark(a) = 0{,}25197\text{ mol}$$
$$N(\text{Cu atoms}) = n \times N_A = (0{,}25197)(6{,}02 \times 10^{23}) \checkmark(b) = 1{,}517 \times 10^{23}\text{ atoms}$$
$$N(\text{electrons}) = (1{,}517 \times 10^{23})(2) \checkmark(c) = 3{,}034 \times 10^{23}\text{ electrons}$$
$$Q = N(\text{electrons}) \times q_e = (3{,}034 \times 10^{23})(1{,}6 \times 10^{-19}) = 48\,160\text{ C} \quad (\text{or } 48\,544\text{ C})$$
$$t = (5)(60)(60) = 18\,000\text{ s} \checkmark(d)$$
$$I = \frac{Q}{\Delta t} = \frac{48\,160}{18\,000} = 2{,}68\text{ A} \checkmark(e)$$

USING $\text{Cu}^+$:
$$N(\text{electrons}) = (1{,}517 \times 10^{23})(1) \implies Q = 24\,080\text{ C}$$
$$I = \frac{24\,080}{18\,000} = 1{,}34\text{ A}$$

**Exam Technique Note:** Always state the formula first, substitute carefully, and verify that your final answer includes the appropriate units and rounding.
